name: Dagestani Handcuff
keyCorrections: If you only get one wrist: control that wrist and use your other hand to secure the cross-wrist ride or claw ride instead
If they roll out: release the handcuff and take the back as they roll
If they separate their hands: you lost the pinched elbow position — re-pinch and drive forward harder
description: Control both wrists from the back or turtle by pulling the near wrist toward your hip while trapping the far wrist, creating a handcuff-like position that exposes the back for a clean back take.
shortInstruction: From turtle or back control, secure the near wrist and pull it toward your hip. Reach under and grab the far wrist. Squeeze elbows together and drive forward to collapse their posture and expose the back.
summary: The Dagestani handcuff traps both wrists to immobilize the opponent and force back exposure, popularized by Khabib Nurmagomedov and the Dagestani wrestling style. By controlling both wrists together, you prevent the opponent from posting, basing, or framing — the only escape is rolling, which you can counter by following the roll and taking the back.
whyItWorks: Trapping both wrists removes the opponent's ability to post or base — without hands, they cannot push themselves up
Driving forward with elbows pinched collapses their posture and forces their weight onto their head
The handcuff position is extremely difficult to escape because both hands are immobilized in the same grip
The system transitions directly to back control as the opponent collapses
commonMistakes: Grabbing too high on the forearm instead of the wrist joint — a forearm grip can be slipped
Letting the elbows flare apart — pinched elbows are the key to controlling both wrists
Not driving forward — the handcuff alone does not flatten; forward pressure is required to collapse the posture
Releasing too early — maintain the handcuff until the back is fully secured
coachingCues: Hold until the back is secure
safetySummary: Wrist control should be applied to the wrist joint, not the hand — gripping the hand can cause finger injuries
Do not apply sudden downward pressure — this can strain the opponent's wrists or shoulders
If the opponent rolls aggressively, release the handcuff and follow the roll rather than fighting

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The Dagestani handcuff follows a four-step sequence: Secure Near Wrist: Trap Far Wrist → Pinch Elbows → Drive Forward

decisionTree.action: from behind the turtle or back control, grab the opponent's near wrist and pull it toward your hip
reach your other hand under their chest/armpit and grab the far wrist. Both wrists should be held in a stacked position between your hands
squeeze your elbows together against their back. This locks both wrists in place and prevents them from separating

walk your knees forward and drive chest pressure into their back. The forward pressure collapses their posture and forces them either flat (exposing the back) or to roll (which you counter into back control)
lift their wrists slightly (as if handcuffing them) to break their posture

moneyDetails: The Dagestani handcuff is one of the most effective turtle-breaking systems in wrestling and BJJ
It is the signature system of Khabib Nurmagomedov and the Dagestani wrestling school — tested at the highest level
Mastering the handcuff gives you a reliable path from turtle to back control that does not require strength
fixItFast: If you only get one wrist: switch to the cross-wrist ride or claw ride instead
If they roll out: release and take the back — do not fight to maintain the handcuff
If they separate their hands: re-pinch the elbows and drive harder
